newsitem.title: UK: Television chef Rankin stars in ad for Quorn.
newsitem.headline: Television chef Rankin stars in ad for Quorn.

text.p: British celebrity chef Paul Rankin will star in a television commercial for Quorn, a meat replacement product, in an ad campaign designed to show that real men don't have to eat meat.
Marlow Foods on Thursday said it is spending 2.5 million pounds ($4.1 million) in the ad campaign for Quorn.
Rankin, a regular TV guest on "Ready Steady Cook," "Master Chef" and on GMTV, will appear in two separate ads for Quorn designed by Abbott Mead Vickers BBDO.

In one advert Rankin proves that real men don't have to eat meat as a hungry crew of firemen tuck into Quorn lasagne, sausages and mash, and goulash. In the second advert Rankin shows that school dinners can be delicious and healthy as he serves Quorn burgers, Quorn fillets and Quorn nuggets to excited schoolchildren.

Rankin follows footballer Ryan Giggs in promoting Quorn. Previous promoters of Quorn include former England union rugby captain Will Carling and British former Olympics 400 metres hurdles champion Sally Gunnell.

"The use of a well known chef further underlines the taste credential of the brand," David Wilson, marketing director for Marlow Foods, said. "With more than three million households regularly buying the brand, this supports the fact that Quorn products are for all the family and all meal occasions."

Marlow Foods in 1996 had the number one position in the meat alternative market, Wilson said. The company's investment in advertising and marketing is expected to maintain Quorn's No. 1 spot in 1997 and result in further growth in the market place, he said.
The ads will begin airing in February and will run across all networks in Britain for four weeks. The ads are estimated to be seen by 37 million people.
